## Quick Takes on the Cessna SkyCourier UX Concept


September 18, 2026


[PDF Version](https://investors.merlinlabs.com/node/7701/pdf)


*Textron Aviation and Merlin introduced a cargo aircraft concept at the Air, Space & Cyber Conference, illustrating how autonomy changes what an aircraft can be - not just how an airframe can fly.*


*By Merlin Investor Relations*


We believe the Cessna SkyCourier UX concept, introduced with Textron Aviation on September 14 at the Air & Space Forces Association’s Air, Space & Cyber Conference, highlights what our software makes possible, i.e. designs that could not be drawn if a pilot had to sit in them. Our[joint release](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260914611105/en/Textron-Aviation-and-Merlin-Introduce-Cessna-SkyCourier-UX-Concept-Aircraft) describes the concept, the reveal and possible paths forward. Here, we offer three observations on why we believe the announcement matters for the business.


**The partner**


Textron Aviation builds the Cessna, Beechcraft and Hawker lines, and has produced more than half of all general aviation aircraft worldwide ([Textron Aviation](https://www.txtav.com/) ). The SkyCourier is its newest cargo platform, type certified by the FAA in March 2022 and flying today with launch customer FedEx Express ([Textron Aviation, March 2022](https://media.txtav.com/211907-the-next-big-thing-in-flight-has-arrived-cessna-skycourier-twin-utility-turboprop-earns-faa-type-certification/) ).


**An aircraft shaped by autonomy**


In his February letter to shareholders, Matt wrote that cockpits exist to keep humans alive and in control at altitude, and that once autonomy carries those responsibilities, an aircraft can be optimized purely for its mission ([Merlin, February 19, 2026](https://merlinlabs.com/news/a-letter-to-shareholders/) ). The SkyCourier UX is that idea drawn at full scale. One configuration under evaluation replaces the cockpit volume with cargo space and opens the nose for loading straight through the front of the aircraft. Nobody draws an airplane like that if a pilot has to sit in it. As Matt says in the release, the concept explores what an aircraft looks like when it is designed around autonomy and cargo instead of a crew. Consistent with our “one brain, many aircraft” profile, the “brain” here is in development. The airframe work, manufacturing and support that turn a concept into a fleet are the parts Textron already does at scale.


**A proven airframe, a new mission**


The military has taken certified civilian aircraft into demanding service before. The U-28A, deployed by Air Force Special Operations Command since 2006, is a modified single-engine Pilatus PC-12 ([U.S. Air Force fact sheet](https://www.af.mil/About-Us/Fact-Sheets/Display/Article/104607/u-28a-draco/) ). The C-146A Wolfhound, continuously deployed since October 2011, is the military version of the Dornier 328 commuter airliner ([U.S. Air Force fact sheet](https://www.af.mil/About-Us/Fact-Sheets/Display/Article/467729/c-146a-wolfhound/) ). Programs like these exist because a certified aircraft in production arrives with its manufacturing system, support network and service record already built, and we could make the same case for the SkyCourier. Autonomy extends the pattern to missions a crewed aircraft cannot reasonably take. As CEO Matt George noted in the release, contested logistics needs capacity and ability to execute high-risk missions, while lowering crew risk and availability constraints.


Note also that the autonomy in this concept airframe is the same core under development with a defense customer on a much larger airframe - the C-130J under our[Condor product family](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/05/14/3294877/0/en/merlin-unveils-plans-for-ai-powered-autonomy-for-commercial-cargo-aircraft.html) , on an indefinite delivery, indefinite quantity (IDIQ) contract with United States Special Operations Command carrying a ceiling of $105 million,[where we completed the critical design review](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/06/04/3307093/0/en/merlin-successfully-completes-critical-design-review-for-c-130j-autonomy-program-with-ussocom.html) on June 4, 2026.


**What to watch from here**


There will certainly be work ahead - including engineering studies and evaluations necessary to build confidence in autonomous and optionally piloted resupply operations. Stay tuned!.
